sentence: 私はアンです。
mnemonic: わたし sounds like 'want a sushi' — picture yourself pointing at your own chest saying 'I want a sushi', which is exactly how you'd say the word for I.
notes: Can also be read わたくし (very formal) or あたし (feminine, casual). There are rarer readings too.

meaning: you (usually when one doesn't know the person)
sentence: あなたはトムさんですか。
mnemonic: あなた sounds like 'another' — when you point at someone else and say 'another', you mean YOU, not me.

sentence: あなたはトムさんですか。
mnemonic: さん sounds exactly like 'sun' — everyone bows respectfully to Mr Sun, the most polite honorific in the sky.
notes: The most common neutral polite honorific, similar to using 'Mr/Ms' before a name in English.

sentence: 彼はトムさんです。
mnemonic: かれ sounds like 'karate' — picture HE does a karate chop, that's kare, that's him.

sentence: 私はワインが好きです。
mnemonic: すき sounds like 'ski' — imagine saying 'I love to ski', you are fond of it, suki.
notes: Grammatically not a verb, though it's often translated into English as 'to like'.

sentence: あの人はいい人です。
sentence_meaning: That person is a good person.
mnemonic: ひと sounds like 'he-toe' — a PERSON steps on a hot coal and yells 'hee-toh!'

sentence: あの人はいい人です。
sentence_meaning: That person is a good person.
mnemonic: いい is just the sound 'eee' — squeal 'eeee!' with delight because something is good.

sentence: 私はイギリス人です。
mnemonic: じん sounds like the name 'Jin' — a PERSON introduces himself: 'I'm Jin, I'm Nihonjin, a person from Japan.'
notes: Used as a suffix on a country name to mean a person from that country, e.g. 日本人 nihonjin.

sentence: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
mnemonic: にほんご sounds like 'knee-hone-go' — you skin your KNEE, HONE your skills, then GO study the Japanese language.

sentence: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
mnemonic: べんきょう sounds like 'Ben Kyoto' — Ben travels all the way to Kyoto just to study.

sentence: いい本でしたね。
sentence_meaning: It was a good book, wasn't it?
mnemonic: ほん sounds like 'hone' — you read a book to hone your skills.

sentence: これは日本語の本です。
mnemonic: これ sounds like 'core' — you point at the core of an apple and say 'this, right here'.

sentence: A「これは何ですか。」B「本です。」
sentence_meaning: A: What is this?B: It's a book.
mnemonic: なに sounds like 'nanny' — a confused nanny throws up her hands shouting 'WHAT?!'
notes: Can be read either なに or なん depending on what follows.

sentence: それは本です。
mnemonic: それ sounds like 'sore' — you point at a sore wound and say 'that, right there, hurts'.

sentence: あれは何ですか。
mnemonic: あれ sounds like the English word 'are' — pointing far into the distance, you ask 'what ARE those, over there?'

sentence: どれが好きですか。
mnemonic: どれ sounds like 'door' — faced with five doors you ask 'which one?'

sentence: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。
mnemonic: まいにち sounds like 'my knee' — 'my knee aches every single day.'

sentence: これは兄のパソコンです。
sentence_meaning: This is my older brother's personal computer.
mnemonic: あに sounds like 'Annie' — your older brother dresses up as Annie every single year for Halloween.

sentence: 兄がいます。
mnemonic: いる sounds like 'ear' — a rabbit's ear pops up from the grass, proof that it exists, right here.

sentence: ペンがある。
mnemonic: ある sounds like the English word 'are' — 'there ARE rocks scattered over there', for things without life.

sentence: スポーツはあまり好きじゃありません。
mnemonic: あまり sounds like 'a Mary' — 'there's not very much left of Mary's cake.'

sentence: 彼は今、勉強しています。
mnemonic: いま sounds like 'Emma' — 'Emma, come here right now!'

sentence: 今は時間がありません。
mnemonic: じかん sounds like 'Genghis Khan' — Genghis Khan checks the time on his watch before charging into battle.

sentence: 今はあまり時間が無いのです。
sentence_meaning: I don't have much time now.
mnemonic: ない sounds like 'nigh' as in Bill Nye — Bill Nye vanishes into thin air, he simply does not exist anymore.
notes: Often used as the negative form of ある. Worth checking a grammar reference for full usage.

sentence: 山田さんの本はどれですか。この本ですか。
sentence_meaning: Which book is Yamada-san's? Is it this book?
mnemonic: この sounds like 'cone' — you point at an ice cream cone and say 'this one is mine'.

sentence: その本ですか。
mnemonic: その sounds like 'Sonic, no' — Sonic points and says 'that one, not this one'.

sentence: あの本ですか。
mnemonic: あの sounds like 'ah, no' — pointing far away, shaking your head, 'that one there, no not this'.

sentence: どの本ですか。
mnemonic: どの sounds like 'dough, no' — holding a bowl of dough you ask 'which one do I knead first?'

sentence: 兄は毎日テレビを見ます。
sentence_meaning: My older brother watches TV every day.
mnemonic: みる sounds like 'mirror' — you look in a mirror to see yourself.

sentence: テレビを全然見ません。
mnemonic: ぜんぜん is doubled like 'zen zen' — a monk meditates so deeply he feels nothing at all, total zen.

sentence: この本は全然面白くなかった。
sentence_meaning: This book wasn't interesting at all.
mnemonic: おもしろい sounds like 'oh Moe, Shirley' — 'oh Moe, Shirley, this is so interesting!'

sentence: 彼はテニスをします。
mnemonic: する sounds like 'sue' — 'I'll sue you if you don't do it!'

meaning: to become, to result in, to come (to do)
sentence: 日本語の勉強が好きになりました。
sentence_meaning: I have come to like Japanese study.
mnemonic: なる sounds like 'gnarly' — the surfing gets so gnarly it becomes genuinely dangerous.
notes: Has many meanings and shades of use ('to become', 'to result in', 'to come to do') — it takes time to fully absorb.

sentence: 私は日本語の先生になりたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to become a Japanese teacher.
mnemonic: せんせい sounds like 'sensei' from every karate movie — a wise teacher always has something to say.

sentence: コーヒーをください。
mnemonic: ください sounds like 'coo-da-sigh' — kneeling down with a long sigh, 'please... give it to me...'

sentence: あなたの名前を教えてください。
mnemonic: なまえ sounds like 'not my A' — 'that's not my A, that's not my name on this test!'

sentence: あなたの名前を教えてください。
mnemonic: おしえる sounds like 'oh, she'll' — 'oh, she'll teach you everything she knows.'

sentence: ここに本があります。
mnemonic: ここ sounds like 'coco' — 'the cocoa is right here!'

sentence: そこはトイレです。
mnemonic: そこ sounds like 'socket' — 'plug it in there, in that socket.'

sentence: 彼はあそこにいます。
mnemonic: あそこ sounds like 'ah, socket' — pointing further than soko, 'ah, it's over there, past the socket.'

sentence: あの本をどこに置きましたか。
sentence_meaning: Where did you put that book?
mnemonic: どこ sounds like 'dough, coh' — 'where did I put my dough?'

sentence: あの本をどこに置きましたか。
sentence_meaning: Where did you put that book?
mnemonic: おく sounds like 'oak' — you put your coffee cup down on the oak table.

sentence: ここが私の家です。
mnemonic: いえ sounds like 'yeah' — coming home and sighing happily, 'yeahh, home at last.'
notes: Can also be read うち in certain contexts.

sentence: 家に帰ろう。
mnemonic: かえる sounds like 'carry, ooh' — you carry your bags as you return home.

sentence: あなたの話は面白いね。
mnemonic: はなし sounds like 'Hannah, she' — 'Hannah, she told me a whole story.'

sentence: あの人を知っていますか。
mnemonic: しる sounds like 'sure' — 'I'm sure, I know the answer.'

sentence: 彼女の名前を知っていますか。
mnemonic: かのじょ sounds like 'can o' Joe' — your girlfriend brings you a can of coffee every single morning.

sentence: 彼女はララちゃんです。
mnemonic: ちゃん sounds like 'Chan', as in Jackie Chan — you affectionately call your little sister 'Jackie-chan'.
notes: An honorific usually used to show endearment, especially with girls and small children.

sentence: A「山田さんですか。」B「はい。」
sentence_meaning: A: Are you Yamada-san?B: Yes, I am.
mnemonic: はい sounds exactly like 'hi' — someone asks a question, you toss a bale of hay and shout 'yes!'

sentence: A「山田さんですか。」B「いいえ。」
sentence_meaning: A: Are you Yamada-san?B: No, I'm not.
mnemonic: いいえ sounds like 'Eeyore' — gloomy Eeyore always says no to everything.

sentence: 日本のゲームは面白いです。
mnemonic: にほん sounds like 'knee-hone' — you land in Japan, skin your knee, then hone your samurai skills.
notes: Can be read either にほん or にっぽん.

sentence: 学校は日本にあります。
mnemonic: がっこう sounds like 'cuckoo' — a cuckoo clock rings out to end class at school.

sentence: 学校へ行きます。
mnemonic: いく sounds like 'eek!' — 'eek, I have to go!' you yell, dashing off.

sentence: 明日、学校へ行きます。

mnemonic: あした sounds like 'a cheetah' — a cheetah runs so fast it's already tomorrow by the time it stops.

sentence: 明日、来ますか。
mnemonic: くる sounds like 'kangaroo' — a kangaroo hops closer and closer, coming right at you.

sentence: 明日、また来ます。
mnemonic: また sounds like 'matter' — 'it doesn't matter, let's just do it again.'

sentence: 彼女はいつ来ますか。
mnemonic: いつ sounds like 'it's due' — 'when is it due?'

sentence: これがいいと思います。
mnemonic: おもう sounds like 'Oh, Moe' — Moe from behind the bar is always thinking hard about something.

sentence: こうしましょう。
mnemonic: こう sounds like 'coe', as in a coach — a coach demonstrates: 'do it like this.'

sentence: 私もそう思います。
mnemonic: そう sounds like 'so' — 'oh, is that so?'

sentence: あなたはどう思いますか。
mnemonic: どう sounds like 'doe', as in money — 'how much dough do you need?'

sentence: 明日、彼と会います。
mnemonic: あう sounds like 'ow' — you meet someone by literally bumping into them, 'ow!'

sentence: 次はいつ会いましょうか。

sentence: 彼は私の方を見ました。

sentence: 次の方、どうぞ。
mnemonic: かた sounds like 'karate' — you politely refer to 'that person' mid karate kata.

sentence: 彼女はラジオを聞いています。
mnemonic: きく sounds like 'kick, ooh' — you kick the door and someone shouts 'I heard that!'

sentence: トムに聞いて。
mnemonic: きく (same word as hear) sounds like 'kick, ooh' — you kick the door to ask a question loudly.

sentence: A「これでお願いします。」B「はい。」
mnemonic: おねがいします breaks into 'oh, negate, she must' — bowing deeply, 'oh, please don't negate my request, she must grant it.'

sentence: 日本語のニュースが全然分かりませんでした。

sentence: よく分かりました。
mnemonic: よく sounds like 'yolk' — you eat egg yolk well, savoring every bite.

sentence: ジャズのCDをよく聞きます。
sentence_meaning: I listen to Jazz CDs often.
mnemonic: よく (same word as well) sounds like 'yolk' — you eat egg yolk often, it's part of your daily routine.

sentence: よく考えてください。
mnemonic: かんがえる sounds like 'conga, eh, roo' — you do the conga line while carefully considering your next move.

word: ありがとうございます
reading: ありがとうございます

sentence: 昨日、友達に会った。

mnemonic: まち sounds like 'match, ee' — you wander through a small town holding a lit match.

sentence: このカメラは高いですね。

sentence: これがこの町で一番高いビルです。

sentence: これはちょっと高いですね。
mnemonic: ちょっと sounds like 'Charlotte' — 'just a little more, Charlotte!'

meaning: to give (receiver is not in the speaker's group)

sentence_meaning: I will give a present to my friend.
mnemonic: あげる sounds like 'a jaguar' — you give a gift to a stranger while a jaguar watches curiously from afar.

meaning: to give (receiver is in the speaker's group)
sentence: 父が本をくれました。
sentence_meaning: My father gave me a book.
mnemonic: くれる sounds like 'cure, ooh' — someone gives you a cure for your illness, given TO you.

sentence: 色々な物をもらいました。

meaning: to be able to do, to be good at

sentence: その話は本当ですか。
mnemonic: ほんとう sounds like 'hone, tow' — 'is that the truth? I need to hone in and tow the line.'
